hook: Your GTA six preorder was never an eighty dollar purchase. And it gets worse.
hook_alt_candidates: You think GTA six costs seventy-nine ninety-nine. It does not. And it gets worse.
Everyone is hyped for GTA six. Almost nobody counted what it really costs.
angle: Money psychology: the $79.99 sticker price is an anchor. Problem: fans pay the headline number, then the small extras stack up. Agitate: buy Standard at $79.99, later pay the $20 upgrade, and you land at $99.99, exactly the Ultimate price, so 'saving $20' saved nothing. The 'free' month of GTA+ on digital pre-orders can turn into a paid $7.99/month plan if you forget to cancel ($95.88 a year). The 'physical edition' is a download code, no disc. Benny's story: he plans a clean $79.99 launch day, then watches the real total creep up. Payoff: the real cost is the price plus the small choices you do not track; decide your total BEFORE you click buy, and cancel the trial the same day. Not a trend recycle: the angle is Benny's own money-habit take, not a copy of any Short.

facts.claim: Rockstar's official GTA VI page says 'Coming November 19, 2026', platforms PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S; the Vintage Vice City Pack is a pre-order bonus. No 'available now' wording on the page.

Standard Edition is $79.99 (US) and Ultimate Edition is $99.99; Standard buyers can later pay the $20 difference to upgrade. Math: $99.99 - $79.99 = $20.00, and $79.99 + $20 = $99.99, so upgrading later costs exactly the Ultimate price (no saving).
The boxed 'physical edition' is only a download code with no disc in the box (Rockstar Store listing, as reported); same $79.99 price as digital.
Digital pre-orders include one month of GTA+; the PlayStation Store warns it can convert to a paid subscription if not cancelled in time.
GTA+ costs $7.99 per month in the US (raised from $5.99 in 2024, one plan, no annual option). Math: 12 x $7.99 = $95.88 a year.

Combined math for the on-screen total: $79.99 + $20 upgrade = $99.99; $99.99 + 12 months of GTA+ ($95.88) = $195.87 for year one if the trial is never cancelled. Say 'about one hundred ninety-six dollars' with 'about' and show '~$196' OR use exact $195.87 everywhere (Rule A).
GTA 6 slipped from May 26, 2026 to Nov 19, 2026 (two delays in total counting the earlier 2025 window): fans waited, and the date held.

Beat outline (14 beats):
1. HOOK (0-4 s): Benny at a store counter, big sign '$79.99'. Voice: 'Your GTA six preorder was never an eighty dollar purchase. And it gets worse.'
2. PROBLEM named: Benny smiles at the price tag, controller in hand. 'You see seventy-nine ninety-nine and think, easy.'
3. AGITATE 1: the 'physical copy' box is opened and has only a code card inside. 'The box? Just a download code. No disc.' (fact 3)
4. AGITATE 2: a tiny sign 'Ultimate $99.99' pops up, Benny peeks at it. 'Ultimate costs ninety-nine ninety-nine.' (fact 2)
5. AGITATE 3 (the knife twist): Benny picks Standard to save twenty dollars. 'So you buy Standard to save twenty.' Cut: counter adds '+$20 upgrade'.
6. TWIST: later he upgrades. Counter shows $79.99 + $20 = $99.99. 'Then you upgrade later. Total: ninety-nine ninety-nine. Same as Ultimate.' Benny face-palms.
7. AGITATE 4: free trial banner. 'Digital preorders include one free month of GTA plus.' (fact 4)
8. Benny forgets the calendar; a month flips; counter ticks $7.99. 'Forget to cancel and it costs seven ninety-nine a month.'
9. Math beat: calendar spins 12 times, counter lands on $95.88. 'That is ninety-five eighty-eight a year.' Use exact figures everywhere on screen and voice (Rule A).
10. Total reveal: '$99.99 + $95.88 = $195.87'. Voice: 'One hundred ninety-five eighty-seven. For a game you thought was eighty.' (If rounded, say 'about' and show '~'.)

11. STORY PAYOFF: Benny rewinds his own day: he sets a total before buying, writes '$99.99 max' on a sticky note, sets a phone reminder to cancel the trial. 'Benny decides his total before he clicks buy.'
12. RULE 1: 'Pick your edition once, not twice.' Sticky note on screen.
13. RULE 2: 'Cancel the trial the same day.' Phone reminder pops.
14. ENDING / comment bait: Benny happy at launch day screen (generic, no game footage), 'Did you buy Standard or Ultimate? Tell me in the comments.' End the moment the question is asked.
Keep every on-screen number identical to the voice (Rules A and C). Caption shows heard words (Rule B).
